solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Earlier prototype of the C5, say?

indicators.note: say tells you to speak the letter-and-digit code aloud

parts.note: the model preceding a C5 would be B4, one letter and one number back, as with Sinclair's C5 electric car

explanation.surface: A question about what came before Clive Sinclair's ill-fated C5 electric tricycle.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sinclair C5 was a notorious 1985 British battery-powered trike. Step each part of 'C5' back one place and you get B4, which spoken sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something happening earlier happened at a prior time.

clue.text: He chops wood to place barrels on top like Guido Fawkes?

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting barrels on top means its letter comes first

parts.note: b is a standard abbreviation for barrel(s)
a lumberjack who fells trees is a logger

explanation.surface: A woodcutter stacking gunpowder barrels, as the original Guy Fawkes did under Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on top' puts B above LOGGER in this down entry. 'Guido Fawkes' is the pen name of a well-known British political gossip website writer, not the 1605 plotter.
explanation.definitionFit: Guido Fawkes is the pseudonym used by Paul Staines for his political website, so he is an example of someone writing online.

clue.text: It's said conspirator shed tools

indicators.note: it's said signals that a word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Guy Fawkes was the best-known conspirator of the 1605 Gunpowder Plot

explanation.surface: A rumour that some plotter has shed his tools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like a verb (discarded) but is a garden shed, qualifying 'tools'. In a non-rhotic British accent the plotter's surname and the answer sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Garden forks are digging implements usually kept in the garden outbuilding.

clue.text: Soldiers mounting revolution in attempt to save the world?

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers; mounting just places them on top in this down entry
one complete turn is a cycle

explanation.surface: Troops staging an uprising as a bid to save the planet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' suggests a political uprising, but it is a turn of a wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: Reusing waste materials is an environmental effort, loosely an attempt to rescue the planet.

clue.text: OOMPH?! That's shocking!

definitions.meaning: read as 00 mph, zero miles per hour, so not moving at all
electricity built up on a surface that gives a small jolt when touched

explanation.surface: An exclamation about something with startling oomph.
explanation.walkthrough: OOMPH is read as 0 0 MPH, a speed of zero, meaning motionless.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: motionless, as at zero speed, and the charge that gives a small electric jolt.

clue.text: Firestarter caught in derailed plot by undercover characters…

indicators.note: letters lying concealed within the run of words caught in derailed are the ones to take

explanation.surface: An arsonist nabbed after a botched conspiracy by secret agents, running on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot by' is linking padding in the surface. 'undercover characters' means letters concealed inside 'caught in derailed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry kindling material is used to get a fire going, so it starts fires.

clue.text: …unfortunately he will rot at place of execution

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things going wrong, so the letters of he will rot are jumbled

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: the arsonist will sadly die and decay at the scaffold.
explanation.walkthrough: Tower Hill, by the Tower of London, was where many traitors were beheaded.
explanation.definitionFit: The open ground beside the Tower of London was a historic site for public beheadings.

clue.text: Barracks here where he laces explosive?

indicators.note: explosive suggests blowing apart, so the letters of he laces are scattered

explanation.surface: A bomber lacing the military barracks with explosives.
explanation.walkthrough: Chelsea Barracks was an army barracks in west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Chelsea Barracks stood in this district of London, so the district is where the barracks were.

clue.text: Gunpowder plot?

parts.note: gunpowder is a type of green tea rolled into pellets, and a plot is a piece of ground where it might be grown

explanation.surface: The 1605 scheme to blow up Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: The famous historical conspiracy is a red herring: gunpowder is a Chinese green tea, and a plot is land for growing it.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate where leaves for brewing are grown could be called a plot of gunpowder.

clue.text: Concerning lack in French director's cinematic style

indicators.note: lack means doing without, so the word for concerning is removed from the director

parts.note: Jean Renoir was a celebrated French film director
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A French director's film style lacking something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lack' takes RE (concerning) out of RENOIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Film noir is a dark, moody genre of crime movie, so the word names a style of film.

clue.text: Can we sleep around? That's when you get everything going

indicators.note: around suggests moving things about, so the letters of can we sleep are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about sleeping around, with a rejoinder about getting everything going.
explanation.definitionFit: A total victory or complete removal, where every prize or item goes, sweeping the board.

clue.text: Pack goods in carton before returning to pocket

indicators.note: to pocket means the case swallows the goods, holding them inside
returning means the assembled letters are read backwards

parts.note: a pack is a case
G is good, so two of them for goods

explanation.surface: Instructions for putting groceries in a box before stowing it away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goods' is two Gs, G being the usual abbreviation for good. 'Pack' looks like a verb but is a noun, a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A silken pouch in which a spider keeps its eggs works as a natural container for them.

clue.text: Pictures crumbles that might appear on The Great British Bake Off

definitions.text: that might appear on The Great British Bake Off

indicators.note: crumbles means breaks up, so the letters of pictures fall apart and re-form

explanation.surface: Pictures of crumble desserts on a TV baking contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumbles' looks like a pudding but is the verb, breaking up 'Pictures'. The Great British Bake Off is a popular UK TV baking competition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastry shells for pies are typical bakes judged on the TV baking contest.

clue.text: Original sin recorded at the beginning of history

indicators.note: recorded suggests something heard on tape, so the phrase is taken by sound

parts.note: an original sin is a prime evil, the first wickedness

explanation.surface: The first sin, written down at the dawn of history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Original sin' becomes prime (first) evil, and 'recorded' says to say it aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Something from the earliest ages of the world dates from the dawn of time.

clue.text: Remembered some dire criminal around the fifth of November

indicators.note: around means the jumbled letters enclose the picked letter
criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters of some dire are twisted
the fifth of picks the fifth letter of November rather than a date

explanation.surface: Recalling a dreadful offence around Bonfire Night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the fifth of November' looks like the date of the Gunpowder Plot but means its fifth letter, M. 'around' puts the anagram of SOME DIRE about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Committed to memory, learnt by heart, so recalled.

clue.text: Card giving you access to capital?

definitions.meaning: a well-known brand of credit card
an entry permit stamped in a passport lets you into a country and its capital city

explanation.surface: A card giving you access to money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' seems to be money, as for a credit card, but the second reading is a capital city entered with a travel permit.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a payment card brand and an official travel permit go by this name.

clue.text: Drop charge

definitions.meaning: to release an explosive from an aircraft
an explosive charge, a device that blows up

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like one phrase, a depth charge dropped from a plane, but splits into two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to attack from the air; as a noun it is an explosive device.

clue.text: It burns primarily alight

indicators.note: primarily means taking the first letter of burns

parts.note: alight means burning, on fire

explanation.surface: A description of something that burns, mostly alight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' takes B from 'burns'; the whole clue also describes the answer, as a heap set alight.
explanation.definitionFit: A large outdoor heap that burns, especially on 5 November in Britain, is first and foremost alight.

clue.text: Novelly structure society with Conservative policy?

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party
a party line is its policy

explanation.surface: A novel structure for society under Tory policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novelly' is a coinage meaning 'in a novel': the plot structure of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: The plot of a novel is the narrative frame that shapes the book's events.

clue.text: Written up 20 lines about V for Vendetta

indicators.note: in a down clue, written up means the letters are read upward, so backwards
about means the den goes round the V

parts.note: 20 points to the clue at 20-down, an underground chamber, here taken as a lair
RY is short for railway, a set of lines

explanation.surface: Twenty lines written about the film V for Vendetta.
explanation.walkthrough: '20' is a cross-reference, not a number: 20-down's underground chamber gives LAIR. LAIR 'about' V, 'Written up', gives RIVAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-running feud is a state of hostile competition between parties.

clue.text: Group in capital on November the fifth caught in a rain storm

indicators.note: capital on means the capital, the first letter, of November
caught in means the fifth is held inside the stormy letters
storm suggests turbulence, so the letters of a rain are tossed about

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: A band visiting the capital on Bonfire Night, caught in a downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'November the fifth' looks like the date but is N plus V. 'caught in' puts V inside IRANA, the anagram of A RAIN that 'storm' makes.
explanation.definitionFit: Nirvana was the Seattle grunge band fronted by Kurt Cobain.

clue.text: Incomplete nerve agent initially strewn about first underground chamber

indicators.note: first places the circa abbreviation ahead of the jumbled letters

parts.note: C stands for circa, about

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of agent
strewn suggests scattered, so the letters are rearranged
incomplete means the last letter of nerve is dropped

explanation.surface: A nerve agent, part used, scattered about an underground room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incomplete' cuts NERVE to NERV; 'initially' adds A; 'strewn' turns NERVA into AVERN; 'about' gives C, placed 'first'.
explanation.definitionFit: A large hollow in rock beneath the surface is a natural underground room.

clue.text: Trendy TV drama aired on time without fail

parts.note: in means fashionable
ER is the American hospital drama series
a programme that was broadcast ran

explanation.surface: A fashionable TV drama broadcast on schedule without fail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aired' means broadcast, so RAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Being incapable of error means never failing or going wrong.

clue.text: This'll make you an upstanding member in the Netherlands, perhaps?

definitions.text: This'll make you an upstanding member in the Netherlands, perhaps?

parts.words: This'll make you an upstanding member in the Netherlands, perhaps
parts.note: the nether lands are the lower regions of the body, and an upstanding member there is an erection

explanation.surface: Something that turns you into a respectable Dutch citizen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upstanding member' looks like a respectable citizen and 'the Netherlands' like Holland; read crudely, they are an erection in the nether regions.
explanation.definitionFit: The impotence drug produces an erection in the lower body, a rude reading of the phrase.

clue.text: Place first couple of Catherine Wheels to create fireworks display?

indicators.note: wheels means turns round, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: to put is to place

indicators.note: first couple of takes the opening two letters of Catherine

explanation.surface: Setting off some Catherine wheels to make a firework show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catherine Wheels' looks like the spinning firework, but 'Wheels' is a verb meaning turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: To misbehave or throw a tantrum is figuratively to put on a fiery show.

clue.text: Sell iodine compound for application in sport

indicators.note: a compound is a mixture, so the letters of sell iodine are mixed

explanation.surface: Marketing an iodine compound for use in sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound' looks like a chemical noun but is the anagram signal. The oil was traditionally rubbed into cricket bats, cricket being a British bat-and-ball game.
explanation.definitionFit: Flax-seed oil is rubbed into willow cricket bats to condition them.

clue.text: Eats shoots and leaves

indicators.note: shoots means darts about, so the letters of eats move around

explanation.surface: The famous panda joke: eats, shoots and leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is the punctuation joke about a panda; 'shoots' is a verb rearranging 'Eats', and 'leaves' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dried leaves of the plant are brewed as drinks, and teas can mean such leaves.

clue.text: Loss of capital in banking sector ultimately

indicators.note: loss of capital means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: banking is the business of lending money

explanation.surface: Losing money in the banking sector in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banking sector' looks like one phrase, but 'banking' gives LENDING and 'sector ultimately' is the definition: the last part of the word sector.
explanation.definitionFit: The final part of something is its close; ultimately the end of the word sector is its tail.

clue.text: Seeing problem in Rorschach's work having originally inserted answer

parts.note: the setter, Rorschach, speaking of himself says my
op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: originally means the first letter of inserted

explanation.surface: An eyesight problem in the setter's inkblot test, the Rorschach being a famous inkblot test.
explanation.walkthrough: Rorschach is this puzzle's setter, so 'Rorschach's' is MY.
explanation.definitionFit: Short-sightedness is a condition in which distant things look blurred.
